outline: Engineering analysis involves the application of scientific methods to understand the state of a system. An engineering system often cannot be dissembled for inspection of individual parts. It is crucial to be able to pinpoint the cause of problems by considering the performance and response of the whole system. This course will start with an introduction to the concepts of scientific research and scientific methods. Keys to access and understand academic research results will then be discussed. During the length of the class, students will have the chance to have first-hand experiences with problem-solving using scientific methods. The class will be concluded with example discussions in the fields of water resources and structural analyses. Students are expected to apply the principles of scientific analyses in future problem solving and discover proper academic research results to assist such problem-solving.
schedule:
1. What is academic research?
2. How are research results disseminated?
3. Research methods - induction and deduction
4. Case study - water resources
5. Case study - earthquake resistant design principles and methods
6. Case study - wind-resistant design principles and methods
7. Case study - quality control of structural materials
assessment:
Attendance and class participation (30%)
Assignments (20%)
Final Report (50%)
